claims.claim: Bodie was a ghost town by 1915
claims.quote: Bodie was first described as a "ghost town" in 1915.

claims.claim: Bodie is in California
claims.quote: Bodie ( BOH-dee) is a ghost town in the Bodie Hills east of the Sierra Nevada mountain range in Mono County, California, United States.

claims.claim: Interiors of Bodie's buildings are still stocked with goods
claims.quote: Interiors remain as they were left and stocked with goods.

claims.claim: About 110 structures survive
claims.quote: Only a small part of the town survived, with about 110 structures still standing, including one of many once operational gold mills.

claims.claim: The town is held in "arrested decay"
claims.quote: Today, Bodie is preserved in a state of arrested decay.

claims.claim: Taking a square nail or a china shard from the site is illegal
claims.quote: Littered throughout the park, one can find small shards of china dishes, square nails, and an occasional bottle, but removing these items is illegal.

claims.claim: By 1879 Bodie had about 2,000 buildings and a population of 7,000–10,000
claims.quote: By 1879, Bodie had a population of approximately 7,000–10,000 people and around 2,000 buildings.

claims.claim: Gold was found at Bodie in 1859
claims.quote: Bodie began as a mining camp of little note following the discovery of gold in 1859 by a group of prospectors, including W. S. Bodey.

claims.claim: The Standard Company's 1876 strike turned a quiet camp into a boomtown
claims.quote: In 1876, the Standard Company discovered a profitable deposit of gold-bearing ore, which transformed Bodie from an isolated mining camp comprising a few prospectors and company employees to a Wild West boomtown.

claims.claim: Bodie's Chinatown crossed Main Street
claims.quote: Bodie had a Chinatown, the main street of which ran at a right angle to Bodie's Main Street.

claims.claim: Bodie averages 303 nights a year below freezing
claims.quote: With an average of 303 nights below freezing per year, Bodie rivals Utqiagvik, Alaska's 315, and no month has ever been completely frost-free.

claims.claim: The record low at Bodie is −36°F
claims.quote: the record low of −36 °F (−37.8 °C) was set on February 13, 1903

claims.claim: Winds cross the valley at close to 100 mph
claims.quote: Winds can sweep across the valley at close to 100 miles per hour (160 km/h).

claims.claim: The last mine closed in 1942 by war order
claims.quote: The last mine closed in 1942, due to War Production Board order L-208, shutting down all non-essential gold mines in the United States during World War II.

claims.claim: The story of Rosa May being buried outside the cemetery fence is unproven/unsubstantiated
claims.quote: There is an unsubstantiated story of Rosa May, a prostitute who, in the style of Florence Nightingale, came to the aid of the town menfolk when a serious epidemic struck the town at the height of its boom.

claims.claim: Rosa May is said to have nursed the town through an epidemic
claims.quote: She is credited with giving life-saving care to many, but after she died she was buried outside the cemetery fence.

claims.claim: Gold was found in the Bodie Hills
claims.quote: Bodie ( BOH-dee) is a ghost town in the Bodie Hills east of the Sierra Nevada mountain range in Mono County, California, United States.

claims.claim: Decline began in 1880
claims.quote: The first signs of decline appeared in 1880 and became obvious toward the end of the year.

claims.claim: Booms in Butte, Tombstone and Utah drew the single miners away
claims.quote: Promising mining booms in Butte, Montana; Tombstone, Arizona; and Utah lured men away from Bodie. The get-rich-quick, single miners who came to the town in the 1870s moved on to these other booms

claims.claim: The last newspaper was printed in 1912
claims.quote: The first signs of an official decline occurred in 1912 with the printing of the last Bodie newspaper, The Bodie Miner.

claims.claim: Mining never resumed after the war
claims.quote: Mining never resumed after the war.

claims.claim: In 1892 the Standard Company built a hydroelectric plant about 13 miles away
claims.quote: In 1892, the Standard Company built its own hydroelectric plant approximately 13 miles (20.9 km) away at Dynamo Pond.

claims.claim: The plant sent 3,530 volts to the company's 20-stamp mill
claims.quote: The plant developed a maximum of 130 horsepower (97 kW) and 3,530 volts alternating current (AC) to power the company's 20-stamp mill.

claims.claim: It was the country's first long-distance transmission of electricity
claims.quote: This pioneering installation marked the country's first transmissions of electricity over a long distance.

claims.claim: Bodie sits at 8,379 feet
claims.quote: at an elevation of 8,379 feet (2,554 m)

claims.claim: Bodie is today a state park
claims.quote: Also registered as a California Historical Landmark, the ghost town officially was established as Bodie State Historic Park in 1962.

claims.claim: The legend that Bodie was California's second or third largest city in 1880 is contradicted by that year's census
claims.quote: One legend says that in 1880, Bodie was California's second or third largest city, but the U.S. Census of that year disproves this.
